mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers a flight to quality in equities, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based consumer demand slowdown, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 110 for three months signals strong economic momentum that leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO is above 110, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment trend (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market discounts future growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS has increased for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate cash flows and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a rising employment trend (PAYEMS) signals a labor market recovery that leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of high-unemployment recovery periods when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.
